Learn more about it.” Watch more by tapping the link in our bio. #clarencethomas #supremecourt #civicengagement #civics #cspanC-SPAN8.2K views · 54m ago1:37White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt announced Wednesday that plans for President Trump’s triumphal arch will be submitted Thursday, with construction slated to begin later this year. “The United States Triumphal Arch will be outfitted with beautiful artwork and depictions celebrating the success of the American people over our 250-year history and the enduring triumph of the American spirit,” she told reporters. “Long after everyone is gone in this room, our children and our grandchildren will remain inspired by this national monument.” The monument is planned for Memorial Circle on Columbia Island in Washington, DC, and designed at a colossal 250 feet in recognition of America’s 250th anniversary. “Great nations build beautiful structures that cultivate national pride and love of country, and this triumphal arch should be a project that all Americans, all political persuasions, can support.” Watch more by tapping the link in our bio. #triumphalarch #potus #washingtondc #cspanC-SPAN32.3K views · 3h ago2:14White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said the U.S. has not requested an extension of the two-week ceasefire with Iran set to expire next week, but that talks between the two countries remain ongoing. “At this moment, we remain very much engaged in these negotiations,” she told reporters Wednesday. “These conversations are productive and ongoing.” The press secretary said “we feel good” about the prospects for a longer-term deal and that it would “obviously” be in Iran’s best interest to “meet the president’s demands.” “I think he’s made his red lines in these negotiations very clear to the other side, and so we are continuing to see how these conversations go,” she said. Ms. Leavitt said there are “discussions” about holding another in-person meeting, which she said would “very likely” again take place in Islamabad, praising the Pakistanis for their role as mediator. “The Pakistanis have been incredible mediators throughout this process,” she said. “They are the only mediator in this negotiation. While there have been many countries around the world who want to offer their help, the president feels it’s important to continue to streamline this communication through the Pakistanis.” The press secretary also declined to provide a timeline for how long the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports would last, but made clear that U.S. forces are only restricting vessels that would benefit Iran’s economy. “We are supporting the freedom of navigation, just not with respect to any tanker or vessel that would benefit the economy of Iran as these negotiations continue,” she said. The U.S. military said overnight that it had “fully implemented” the blockade, with more than 10,000 soldiers, as well as dozens of planes and warships, being used for enforcement. Within the first 48 hours, American warships issued warnings to nine vessels, prompting them to turn around, U.S. Central Command said. In response to the U.S. blockade, Iran’s military threatened to halt all shipping in the region. Eric Swalwell (D-CA), who resigned from Congress Tuesday amid accusations of sexual misconduct. “I think it’s also quite plausible … that there were many other Democrats in this town, on Capitol Hill, who knew about his, perhaps illegal behavior, certainly his disgusting and inappropriate behavior, and why were they silent for so long?” she said. Watch more by tapping the link in our bio. #leavitt #swalwell #politics #congress #cspanC-SPAN25.6K views · 5h ago2:59Sen. Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) criticized President Trump in an emotional speech on Wednesday as she introduced a war powers resolution to limit the president’s ability to wage war against Iran. “I’m here today under this great Capitol dome to keep that most sacred oath, because right now, thousands of our troops are ready to do their jobs, even if it means laying down their lives,” she said. “It’s tragic — it’s disgusting — to me that even as they prepare to do their jobs, our president and some members of this chamber seem so eager to neglect their own.” Sen. Duckworth served as an Army helicopter pilot during the Iraq War, in which her aircraft was shot down, costing her both of her legs. She retired from the armed forces in 2014. “I know what it’s like and what is at stake for the troops this administration is sending into harm’s way,” Sen. Duckworth said. “We must safeguard their valor and their professionalism by doing our jobs.” Watch more by tapping the link in our bio. #iran #trump #politics #illinois #democrats cspanC-SPAN15.6K views · 6h ago2:35Speaker Mike Johnson (R-LA) vowed Wednesday to “exact punishment” on “predators” in Congress following the resignations of Reps. Eric Swalwell (D-CA) and Tony Gonzales (R-TX) amid sexual misconduct scandals. “The question is what more could the House do to protect staffers from predators. You didn’t say that, I said it,” the speaker said at a press conference. “Look, some of the allegations that have been made, and apparently some of the facts that are coming out to verify those allegations, are shocking to us as they are to all of you, and they must be addressed.” The speaker said the House had “tightened up” ethics rules and that leadership would “continue to be as aggressive as possible” to ensure lawmakers comply with rules and laws. “We will bring exact punishment upon those who violate that sacred obligation they have to be a good steward and a boss over their staffs and to not use that position for that kind of terrible activity,” he said. “I don’t know what else to say about it other than it’s detestable.” The two lawmakers resigned from the House on Tuesday, avoiding potential attempts to expel them from Congress after Mr. Gonzales admitted to having an affair with a staffer, who later died by self-immolation, and numerous women accused Mr. Swalwell of sexual assault. Speaker Johnson also noted that the Ethics Committee would soon vote on a punishment for Rep. Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick (D-FL) after finding her guilty of dozens of ethics violations, and said he supported her expulsion from the chamber. “I suspect that that may be expulsion. In my view, that would be appropriate there,” he said. “It is a rare penalty. It’s only happened so far six times since 1789, but these times call for desperate measures, right?” Watch more by tapping the link in our bio. #mikejohnson #tonygonzalez #ericswalwell #cspanC-SPAN166.8K views · 6h ago9:19White House Budget Director Russell Vought said President Trump’s FY 2027 budget request would continue the administration’s push to reduce government spending as he testified before the House Budget Committee. “Under President Trump’s bold leadership, every tool in the executive fiscal toolbox has been used to achieve real savings, and our administration will continue to do so,” he told lawmakers Wednesday. The proposal includes additional cuts to federal grants and research funding, building on reductions in last year’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act. It also calls for $1.5 trillion in Defense Department funding — a 40% increase over current levels. Protestors interrupted Mr. Vought’s opening remarks with chants and signs declaiming the White House’s attempts to end funding for the PEPFAR program that provides HIV/AIDS relief in sub-Saharan Africa. Watch more by tapping the link in our bio. #russellvought #trump #politics #cspanC-SPAN4.8K views · 7h ago4:21Vice President JD Vance on Tuesday said he welcomes when the pope speaks on certain issues because it sparks discussion, but warned Pope Leo XIV to be “careful” when he opines on “matters of theology.” Pope Leo, the first American pontiff, has become increasingly vocal in his opposition to the Iran war, drawing the ire of President Trump, who branded him “weak on crime” and “terrible on foreign policy.” The vice president, a Catholic, took particular issue with the pope’s declaration that the followers of Jesus are “never on the side of those who once wielded the sword and today drop bombs.” “Was God on the side of the Americans who liberated France from the Nazis?” the vice president said at a Turning Point USA event at the University of Georgia. “I certainly think the answer is yes.” Vice President Vance said that if the pope is going to speak on “matters of theology,” it’s important that his comments are “anchored in the truth.” “In the same way that it’s important for the vice president of the United States to be careful when I talk about matters of public policy, I think it’s very, very important for the pope to be careful when he talks about matters of theology,” he said.
